name: batch_modify_gmail_message_labels
title: Batch Modify Gmail Message Labels
description:
Adds or removes labels from multiple Gmail messages in a single batch request.

Takes MESSAGE ids, not thread ids. Gmail's batch endpoint returns no
per-message result and silently ignores ids it does not recognise, so by
default this reads the messages back afterwards and reports which ids
actually changed.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

message_ids.description: A list of message IDs to modify.

add_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to add to the messages.

remove_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to remove from the messages.

verify.description:
Read the messages back and report per-id outcomes. Costs
one extra (batched) read per id. Set False for very large sweeps
where that cost matters and an unverified result is acceptable.

name: create_calendar
title: Create Calendar
description: Creates a new secondary Google Calendar.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

summary.description: The title/name of the new calendar.

description.description: An optional description for the calendar.

name: draft_gmail_message
title: Draft Gmail Message
description:
Creates a draft email in the user's Gmail account. Supports both new drafts and reply drafts with optional attachments.
Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to draft from configured alias addresses.

SCHEDULED SEND IS NOT AVAILABLE. Gmail's REST API exposes no send-time
parameter; the Schedule send feature is web-UI only, and a message cannot be
placed in the Scheduled folder through the API. Do not claim a message was
scheduled. To deliver at a chosen time, create a draft with
draft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to
create and send a new message via send_gmail_message then, or call
users.drafts.send with the draft ID returned by draft_gmail_message.
Alternatively, let the user schedule the draft in the Gmail UI.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.

body_format.description: Email body format. Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the account's default Send As address, falling back to the authenticated user's email when Gmail returns no usable Send-As entry or settings access is not authorized.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: 'url' (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR 'path' (file path, auto-encodes), OR 'content' (standard base64, not urlsafe) + 'filename'. Optional 'mime_type'. Optional 'content_id' (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment.

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the original message as a quoted reply. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

name: get_events
title: Get Events
description:
Retrieves events from a specified Google Calendar. Can retrieve a single event by ID or multiple events within a time range.
You can also search for events by keyword by supplying the optional "query" param.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar to query. Use 'primary' for the user's primary calendar. Defaults to 'primary'. Calendar IDs can be obtained using `list_calendars`.

event_id.description: The ID of a specific event to retrieve. If provided, retrieves only this event and ignores time filtering parameters.

time_min.description: The start of the time range (inclusive) in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2024-05-12T10:00:00Z' or '2024-05-12'). If omitted, defaults to the current time when single_events=True. It is omitted from unexpanded queries so recurring masters that began in the past but still have future occurrences remain discoverable. Ignored if event_id is provided.

time_max.description: The end of the time range (exclusive) in RFC3339 format. If omitted, events starting from `time_min` onwards are considered (up to `max_results`). Ignored if event_id is provided.

max_results.description: The maximum number of events to return in one page. Defaults to 25. Ignored if event_id is provided.

query.description: A keyword to search for within event fields (summary, description, location). Ignored if event_id is provided.

detailed.description: Whether to return detailed event information including description, location, colour (colorId), attendees, and attendee details (response status, organizer, optional flags). Recurring instances also report the parent series ID needed to edit the whole series; recurring masters report their raw RFC5545 recurrence rules; and events that are not ordinary confirmed meetings report their event type (outOfOffice, workingLocation, focusTime) and status. Defaults to False.

include_attachments.description: Whether to include attachment information in detailed event output. When True, shows attachment details (fileId, fileUrl, mimeType, title) for events that have attachments. Only applies when detailed=True. Set this to True when you need to view or access files that have been attached to calendar events, such as meeting documents, presentations, or other shared files. Defaults to False.

single_events.description: Whether to expand recurring series into individual instances. Defaults to True for backwards compatibility. Set to False with detailed=True to retrieve recurring master events and their exact RFC5545 recurrence rules instead of inferring cadence from expanded instances.

page_token.description: Token for the next page, taken from a previous response. When single_events=True, also pass the response's Pagination time_min as time_min, even if omitted on the first call. Keep all other query parameters unchanged. Ignored if event_id is provided.

name: get_gmail_attachment_content
title: Get Gmail Attachment Content
description:
Downloads an email attachment and saves it to local disk.

In stdio mode, returns the local file path for direct access.
In HTTP mode, returns a temporary download URL (valid for 1 hour).
May re-fetch message metadata to resolve filename and MIME type.

message_id.description: The ID of the Gmail message containing the attachment.

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to download.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

return_base64.description:
When True, includes the full attachment as a
standard base64 string in the response (in addition to any file
path or download URL). Useful for sandboxed clients that cannot
reach localhost download URLs or the MCP server's local file
paths (e.g. containerized agents with network allowlists). The
returned base64 uses the standard alphabet, so it can be passed
directly to tools like ``draft_gmail_message`` that expect
standard (not URL-safe) base64. Default False preserves the
existing behavior and response size.

attachment_index.description:
Zero-based attachment position from
the message-content response. When the cap is enabled, this lets
the server safely resolve Gmail's refreshed attachment IDs against
current metadata before downloading.

name: get_gmail_message_content
title: Get Gmail Message Content
description:
Retrieves the full content (subject, sender, recipients, body) of a specific Gmail message.

Bodies are returned inline and truncated at 20,000 characters. Set full=True to
get the complete, untruncated message instead: it is exported to disk and the
response carries a short-lived download URL (HTTP transport) or file path (stdio
transport) rather than the body, so large messages never stream through the model
context. Stateless deployments have no file storage, so there full=True returns the
untruncated body inline.

message_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail message to retrieve.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

full.description: When True, return the COMPLETE untruncated message: saved to local storage and referenced by download URL/file path instead of the body text, or inlined in the response when the server has no file storage (stateless mode). Use for messages large enough to hit the truncation limit, or when byte-exact fidelity is needed (pair with body_format='raw' for a .eml export).

format.description:
Message format. "full" (default) includes
the body and attachments, "metadata" only headers.

name: get_gmail_messages_content_batch
title: Get Gmail Messages Content Batch
description:
Retrieves the content of multiple Gmail messages in a single batch request.
Supports up to 25 messages per batch to prevent SSL connection exhaustion.

message_ids.description: List of Gmail message IDs to retrieve (max 25 per batch).

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

format.description: Message format. "full" includes body, "metadata" only headers.

body_format.description: Body output format (only applies when format='full'). 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches the full raw MIME message and returns the base64url-decoded content.

name: get_gmail_thread_content
title: Get Gmail Thread Content
description:
Retrieves the complete content of a Gmail conversation thread, including all messages.

Optionally also returns structured ownership analysis so a caller can
determine who sent the last message and who owes whom a response without
re-parsing the formatted string or making a second tool call.

thread_id.description: The unique ID of the Gmail thread to retrieve.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format. 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches each message's full raw MIME content and returns the base64url-decoded body.

include_analysis.description: When True, the return value is a dict with both the formatted thread content AND structured ownership analysis (last sender, ball-in-court verdict, per-sender message counts, participants). Defaults to False, in which case the existing string return shape is preserved.

name: get_gmail_threads_content_batch
title: Get Gmail Threads Content Batch
description:
Retrieves the content of multiple Gmail threads in a single batch request.
Supports up to 25 threads per batch to prevent SSL connection exhaustion.

thread_ids.description: A list of Gmail thread IDs to retrieve. The function will automatically batch requests in chunks of 25.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

body_format.description: Body output format. 'text' (default) returns plaintext (HTML converted to text as fallback). 'html' returns the raw HTML body as-is without conversion. 'raw' fetches each message's full raw MIME content and returns the base64url-decoded body.

name: get_task
title: Get Task
description: Get details of a specific task.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list containing the task.

task_id.description: The ID of the task to retrieve.

name: get_task_list
title: Get Task List
description: Get details of a specific task list.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list to retrieve.

name: list_calendars
title: List Calendars
description: Retrieves a list of calendars accessible to the authenticated user.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

max_results.description: Maximum calendars to return in one page. Omit to use the API default.

page_token.description: Token for the next page, taken from a previous response.

name: list_gmail_filters
title: List Gmail Filters
description: Lists all Gmail filters configured in the user's mailbox.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

name: list_gmail_labels
title: List Gmail Labels
description: Lists labels in the user's Gmail account.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

prefix.description:
Return only labels whose name starts with this
exact (case-sensitive) string. users.labels.list accepts no filter,
so the full list is fetched and narrowed here: this shrinks what the
caller receives, not the API call.

include_system.description:
Include Gmail system labels (INBOX, SENT, ...).
Set False to return user labels only.

name: list_task_lists
title: List Task Lists
description: List all task lists for the user.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

max_results.description: Maximum number of task lists to return (default: 1000, max: 1000).

name: list_tasks
title: List Tasks
description: List all tasks in a specific task list.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list to retrieve tasks from.

max_results.description: Maximum number of tasks to return. (default: 20, max: 10000).

show_completed.description: Whether to include completed tasks (default: True). Note that show_hidden must also be true to show tasks completed in first party clients, such as the web UI and Google's mobile apps.

show_deleted.description: Whether to include deleted tasks (default: False).

show_hidden.description: Whether to include hidden tasks (default: False).

show_assigned.description: Whether to include assigned tasks (default: False).

completed_max.description: Upper bound for completion date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

completed_min.description: Lower bound for completion date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

due_max.description: Upper bound for due date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

due_min.description: Lower bound for due date (RFC 3339 timestamp).

updated_min.description: Lower bound for last modification time (RFC 3339 timestamp).

name: manage_event
title: Manage Event
description: Manages calendar events. Supports creating, updating, deleting, and RSVP.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

start_time.description: Start time (required for create). An RFC3339 UTC offset identifies the exact instant and is preserved. Without an offset, supply start_timezone or timezone. For a local wall-clock time, omit the offset and pass the zone so Google resolves daylight saving; a wrong offset moves the event. Date-only values create all-day events.

end_time.description: End time (required for create). An RFC3339 UTC offset identifies the exact instant and is preserved. Without an offset, supply end_timezone or timezone. All-day end dates are exclusive.

event_id.description: Event ID (required for update and delete).

attendees.description: Attendee email addresses, attendee objects (e.g. {"email": ..., "responseStatus": "accepted"}), or a mix of both.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone applied to both boundaries (e.g.,
"America/New_York"). Converts offset-bearing timestamps without changing their
instant; interprets offset-free timestamps as local times in this zone.
Overridden per boundary by start_timezone/end_timezone.

attachments.description:
List of Google Drive file URLs or IDs to attach.
On action="update" this replaces the event's existing attachments rather than
appending to them, matching the Calendar API's patch semantics.

add_google_meet.description: Whether to add/remove native Google Meet.

conference_data.description:
Raw Google Calendar `conferenceData`
payload to attach a third-party conference (Zoom/Webex/Teams add-on). Use this
for full control; mutually exclusive with the conference_provider helper params
and with add_google_meet. (create/update only)

conference_provider.description:
Higher-level helper: third-party provider name
(e.g. "zoom", "webex", "teams"). Requires conference_uri. The MCP builds the
addOn `conferenceData` block internally. (create/update only)

conference_uri.description:
Join URL for the third-party conference (e.g.
"https://zoom.us/j/123456789"). Required when conference_provider is set.

conference_passcode.description: Optional passcode for the third-party conference.

recurrence.description: RFC5545 recurrence rules for a recurring event, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10"].

guests_can_see_other_guests.description: Whether attendees can see other guests.

rsvp_comment.description: Optional message to include with the RSVP response (rsvp action only).

send_updates.description: Notification behavior for create, update, delete, and rsvp — "all" (default), "externalOnly", or "none".

start_timezone.description:
IANA timezone for the start boundary only,
overriding timezone. Use for events whose two ends sit in different zones -
a flight departing 13:45 "Asia/Jerusalem" and landing 17:50
"Europe/Amsterdam" is one event authored in two zones. Explicit timestamp
offsets always preserve the instant, even when the zone differs.

end_timezone.description:
IANA timezone for the end boundary only,
overriding timezone. See start_timezone.

name: manage_focus_time
title: Manage Focus Time
description:
Manages Focus Time events on Google Calendar. These special events auto-decline
meeting invitations and, by default, set the user's chat status to Do Not
Disturb, helping protect blocks of uninterrupted work time.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

start_time.description: Start date/time. Use 'YYYY-MM-DD' for full-day or RFC3339 for partial-day (e.g., '2024-04-05T09:00:00Z'). Date-only values are auto-converted to dateTime (midnight-to-midnight). Required for create.

end_time.description: End date/time (exclusive). Same format as start_time. For a single full day on April 5, use start_time='2026-04-05' and end_time='2026-04-06'. Required for create.

summary.description: Display text on the calendar. Defaults to "Focus Time".

description.description: Event description. Useful for adding context about what the focus time is for.

auto_decline_mode.description: How to handle conflicting invitations. One of: "declineAllConflictingInvitations" (default), "declineOnlyNewConflictingInvitations", "declineNone".

chat_status.description: Google Chat status during the focus time. Supports "doNotDisturb" (default) and "available".

recurrence.description: RFC5545 recurrence rules for a recurring Focus Time series, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10"].

timezone.description: Timezone for the event (e.g., "America/New_York", "Europe/London"). Required when using date-only values or dateTime values without an explicit UTC offset.

time_min.description: For "list" action: start of time range. Defaults to current time. Recurring series are expanded into individual instances in the requested range.

time_max.description: For "list" action: end of time range.

max_results.description: For "list" action: maximum events to return. Defaults to 10.

event_id.description: Event ID. Required for "update" and "delete" actions.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID. Defaults to 'primary'. Focus Time status events live on primary calendars, so use 'primary' or a user's primary calendar ID/email rather than a secondary calendar ID.

name: manage_gmail_filter
title: Manage Gmail Filter
description: Manages Gmail filters. Supports creating and deleting filters.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

filter_action.description: Filter action object (required for create). Named 'filter_action' to avoid shadowing the 'action' parameter.

filter_id.description: ID of the filter to delete (required for delete).

name: manage_gmail_label
title: Manage Gmail Label
description: Manages Gmail labels: create, update, or delete labels.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: Action to perform on the label.

name.description: Label name. Required for create, optional for update.

label_id.description: Label ID. Required for update and delete operations.

label_list_visibility.description: Whether the label is shown in the label list. Defaults to "labelShow" on create. On update, omitting it keeps the label's current setting.

message_list_visibility.description: Whether the label's messages are shown in the message list. Defaults to "show" on create. On update, omitting it keeps the label's current setting.

background_color.description: Label background color as a hex string, e.g. "#fb4c2f". Set together with text_color; Gmail requires both. Gmail accepts only its own palette, and an unsupported value is rejected before the request. Colors apply to user labels, not system labels.

text_color.description: Label text color as a hex string, e.g. "#ffffff". Set together with background_color. Same palette. On update, omitting both keeps the label's current color.

clear_color.description: On update, remove the label's current color. Cannot be combined with background_color or text_color.

name: manage_out_of_office
title: Manage Out of Office
description:
Manages Out of Office events on Google Calendar. These special events auto-decline
meeting invitations and set the user's status to "Out of office" across Google Workspace.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

start_time.description: Start date/time. Use 'YYYY-MM-DD' for full-day or RFC3339 for partial-day (e.g., '2024-04-05T09:00:00Z'). Date-only values are auto-converted to dateTime (midnight-to-midnight). Required for create.

end_time.description: End date/time (exclusive). Same format as start_time. For a single full day on April 5, use start_time='2026-04-05' and end_time='2026-04-06'. Required for create.

summary.description: Display text on the calendar. Defaults to "Out of Office".

auto_decline_mode.description: How to handle conflicting invitations. One of: "declineAllConflictingInvitations" (default), "declineOnlyNewConflictingInvitations", "declineNone".

recurrence.description: RFC5545 recurrence rules for a recurring Out of Office series, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10"].

timezone.description: Timezone for the event (e.g., "America/New_York", "Europe/London"). Required when using date-only values or dateTime values without an explicit UTC offset.

time_min.description: For "list" action: start of time range. Defaults to current time. Recurring series are expanded into individual instances in the requested range.

time_max.description: For "list" action: end of time range.

max_results.description: For "list" action: maximum events to return. Defaults to 10.

event_id.description: Event ID. Required for "update" and "delete" actions.

calendar_id.description: Calendar ID. Defaults to 'primary'. Out of Office status events live on primary calendars, so use 'primary' or a user's primary calendar ID/email rather than a secondary calendar ID.

name: manage_task
title: Manage Task
description: Manage tasks: create, update, delete, or move tasks within task lists.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: The action to perform. Must be one of: "create", "update", "delete", "move".

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list. Required for all actions.

task_id.description: The ID of the task. Required for "update", "delete", and "move" actions.

title.description: The title of the task. Required for "create", optional for "update".

notes.description: Notes/description for the task. Used by "create" and "update" actions.

status.description: Task status ("needsAction" or "completed"). Used by "update" action.

due.description: Due date in RFC 3339 format (e.g., "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"). Used by "create" and "update" actions.

parent.description: Parent task ID (for subtasks). Used by "create" and "move" actions.

previous.description: Previous sibling task ID (for positioning). Used by "create" and "move" actions.

destination_task_list.description: Destination task list ID (for moving between lists). Used by "move" action.

name: manage_task_list
title: Manage Task List
description: Manage task lists: create, update, delete, or clear completed tasks.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

action.description: The action to perform. Must be one of: "create", "update", "delete", "clear_completed".

task_list_id.description: The ID of the task list. Required for "update", "delete", and "clear_completed" actions.

title.description: The title for the task list. Required for "create" and "update" actions.

name: modify_gmail_message_labels
title: Modify Gmail Message Labels
description:
Adds or removes labels from a Gmail message.
To archive an email, remove the INBOX label.
To delete an email, add the TRASH label.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

message_id.description: The ID of the message to modify.

add_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to add to the message.

remove_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to remove from the message.

name: query_freebusy
title: Query Freebusy
description: Returns free/busy information for a set of calendars.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

time_min.description: The start of the interval for the query in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2024-05-12T10:00:00Z' or '2024-05-12').

time_max.description: The end of the interval for the query in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2024-05-12T18:00:00Z' or '2024-05-12').

calendar_ids.description: List of calendar identifiers to query. If not provided, queries the primary calendar. Use 'primary' for the user's primary calendar or specific calendar IDs obtained from `list_calendars`.

group_expansion_max.description: Maximum number of calendar identifiers to be provided for a single group. Optional. An error is returned for a group with more members than this value. Maximum value is 100.

calendar_expansion_max.description: Maximum number of calendars for which FreeBusy information is to be provided. Optional. Maximum value is 50.

name: search_gmail_messages
title: Search Gmail Messages
description:
Searches messages in a user's Gmail account based on a query.
Returns both Message IDs and Thread IDs for each found message, along with Gmail web interface links for manual verification.
Supports pagination via page_token parameter.

query.description: The search query. Supports standard Gmail search operators.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required.

page_size.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 10.

page_token.description: Token for retrieving the next page of results. Use the next_page_token from a previous response.

include_headers.description:
If True, also fetch each message's metadata and include
Subject, From, and Date per result. Costs one metadata get per result,
grouped into HTTP batches of up to 10, plus retries for transient failures.
Defaults to False (output unchanged from prior versions).

name: send_gmail_message
title: Send Gmail Message
description:
Sends an email using the user's Gmail account. Supports new emails, replies, and
forwards, with optional attachments. Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to send
from configured alias addresses.

To forward an existing message, pass forward_message_id. The original subject,
body (quoted with a "Forwarded message" header), and attachments are carried over.
In forward mode, body (if any) is prepended as a note and subject is optional.
Threading, reply, and signature options do not apply when forwarding.

THIS TOOL SENDS IMMEDIATELY AND CANNOT SCHEDULE. Gmail's REST API exposes no
send-time parameter; Schedule send is a web-UI feature with no API equivalent,
so no argument to this tool can defer delivery. Never tell a user a message
was scheduled. For "prepare now, deliver later", create a draft with
draft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to
create and send a new message via send_gmail_message at the chosen time, or
call users.drafts.send with the draft ID returned by draft_gmail_message.
Alternatively, let the user schedule that draft in the Gmail UI.

user_google_email.description: The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.

to.description: Recipient email address. Optional when replying with reply_all=True, which derives it from the thread.

subject.description: Email subject. Required when sending; optional when forwarding (defaults to 'Fwd: <original subject>').

body.description: Email body content (plain text or HTML). Required when sending. When forwarding, this is an optional note prepended above the quoted original.

body_format.description: Format of the body content (and of the prepended note when forwarding). Use 'plain' for plaintext or 'html' for HTML content.

forward_message_id.description: Set to a Gmail message ID to forward that message instead of composing a new one. The original subject, body, and (optionally) attachments are carried over; 'body' becomes an optional note prepended to the forward.

include_forwarded_attachments.description: When forwarding, whether to include the original message's attachments. Ignored unless forward_message_id is set.

from_name.description: Optional sender display name (e.g., 'Peter Hartree'). If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.

from_email.description: Optional 'Send As' alias email address. Must be configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided, uses the authenticated user's email.

thread_id.description: Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message with an RFC Message-ID.

in_reply_to.description: Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.

references.description: Optional Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally omit when thread_id is provided; the server derives the chain through the selected reply target.

attachments.description: Optional list of attachments. Each can have: "url" (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR "path" (file path, auto-encodes), OR "content" (standard base64, not urlsafe) + "filename". Optional "mime_type". Optional "content_id" (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: ` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment. Example: [{"url": "https://host/attachments/abc-123", "filename": "report.pdf"}]

include_signature.description: Whether to append the Gmail signature from Settings > Signature when available. Defaults to true.

quote_original.description: Whether to include the message being replied to as a quoted original. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. Defaults to false.

reply_all.description: Whether to derive reply-all recipients from the thread: To = the sender being replied to, Cc = the other participants, excluding the authenticated account and from_email. Requires thread_id. Explicit to/cc win; when cc is omitted the sender being replied to is added to the derived Cc if they are not already in To. Defaults to false.
